claim: The phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-Akt network is tightly controlled by feedback mechanisms that regulate signal flow and ensure signal fidelity.
source: The phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-Akt network is tightly controlled by feedback mechanisms that regulate signal flow and ensure signal fidelity.
evidence: This is a general statement about the PI3K-Akt network that is established knowledge in the field.

claim: A rapid overshoot in insulin-stimulated recruitment of Akt to the plasma membrane has previously been reported.
source: A rapid overshoot in insulin-stimulated recruitment of Akt to the plasma membrane has previously been reported, which is indicative of negative feedback operating on acute timescales.
evidence: This claim references previous reports in the literature.

claim: The overshoot in insulin-stimulated recruitment of Akt to the plasma membrane is indicative of negative feedback operating on acute timescales.
source: A rapid overshoot in insulin-stimulated recruitment of Akt to the plasma membrane has previously been reported, which is indicative of negative feedback operating on acute timescales.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on established knowledge about feedback mechanisms and their characteristic dynamics.

claim: Akt engages negative feedback by phosphorylating insulin receptor substrate (IRS) 1 and 2 on a number of residues.
source: Here, we show that Akt itself engages this negative feedback by phosphorylating insulin receptor substrate (IRS) 1 and 2 on a number of residues.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Phosphorylation of IRS1/2 by Akt results in the depletion of plasma membrane-localised IRS1/2.
source: Phosphorylation results in the depletion of plasma membrane-localised IRS1/2, reducing the pool available for interaction with the insulin receptor.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5 and related experiments.

claim: Depletion of plasma membrane-localised IRS1/2 reduces the pool available for interaction with the insulin receptor.
source: Phosphorylation results in the depletion of plasma membrane-localised IRS1/2, reducing the pool available for interaction with the insulin receptor.
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 5J showing reduced IR-IRS interaction when Akt is active.

claim: Akt-mediated depletion of plasma membrane IRS1/2 limits plasma membrane-associated PI3K.
source: Together these events limit plasma membrane-associated PI3K and phosphatidylinositol (3,4,5)-trisphosphate (PIP3) synthesis.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4F-G showing increased PM PI3K in the presence of Akt inhibitors.

claim: Akt-mediated depletion of plasma membrane IRS1/2 limits phosphatidylinositol (3,4,5)-trisphosphate (PIP3) synthesis.
source: Together these events limit plasma membrane-associated PI3K and phosphatidylinositol (3,4,5)-trisphosphate (PIP3) synthesis.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3A showing increased PIP3 levels when Akt is inhibited.

claim: IRS2 S306 (S303 in mouse) is an Akt-dependent phosphorylation site that is a key driver of negative feedback.
source: We identified two Akt-dependent phosphorylation sites in IRS2 at S306 (S303 in mouse) and S577 (S573 in mouse) that are key drivers of this negative feedback.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro kinase assays, cellular experiments with Akt inhibitors, and functional studies with mutant IRS2 shown in Figure 6.

claim: IRS2 S577 (S573 in mouse) is an Akt-dependent phosphorylation site that is a key driver of negative feedback.
source: We identified two Akt-dependent phosphorylation sites in IRS2 at S306 (S303 in mouse) and S577 (S573 in mouse) that are key drivers of this negative feedback.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro kinase assays, cellular experiments with Akt inhibitors, and functional studies with mutant IRS2 shown in Figure 6.

claim: Akt acutely controls PIP3 abundance through post-translational modification of the IRS scaffold.
source: These findings establish a novel mechanism by which the kinase Akt acutely controls PIP3 abundance, through post-translational modification of the IRS scaffold.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence throughout the manuscript.

claim: Negative feedback loops enable rapid, tightly regulated responses to stimuli and prevent pathway hyperactivation.
source: For example, positive feedback loops facilitate adequate signal amplification, while negative feedback loops enable rapid, tightly regulated responses to stimuli and prevent pathway hyperactivation (Cheong and Levchenko, 2010; Tyson et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Negative feedback ensures that signalling pathways are resistant to external perturbations.
source: Negative feedback also ensures that signalling pathways are resistant to external perturbations (Stelling et al., 2004) and may optimise the energetic cost of signal transduction (Anders et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Negative feedback may optimise the energetic cost of signal transduction.
source: Negative feedback also ensures that signalling pathways are resistant to external perturbations (Stelling et al., 2004) and may optimise the energetic cost of signal transduction (Anders et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Dysfunctional cell signalling frequently underlies complex diseases.
source: Identifying and characterising feedback mechanisms in signal transduction pathways is pivotal since dysfunctional cell signalling frequently underlies complex diseases (Fazakerley et al., 2019; Mora-Garcia and Sakamoto, 1999; Nguyen and Kholodenko, 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Binding of insulin to the insulin receptor (IR) leads to receptor auto-phosphorylation.
source: For example, binding of insulin to the insulin receptor (IR) leads to receptor auto-phosphorylation, and subsequent binding of the insulin receptor substrate (IRS) 1 and 2 adaptors via their phosphotyrosine-binding (PTB) domains (Boucher et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about insulin signaling, supported by a citation.

claim: IRS proteins bind to the insulin receptor via their phosphotyrosine-binding (PTB) domains following insulin receptor auto-phosphorylation.
source: For example, binding of insulin to the insulin receptor (IR) leads to receptor auto-phosphorylation, and subsequent binding of the insulin receptor substrate (IRS) 1 and 2 adaptors via their phosphotyrosine-binding (PTB) domains (Boucher et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: PI3K phosphorylates phosphatidylinositol (4,5) bisphosphate at the plasma membrane to form phosphatidylinositol (3,4,5) trisphosphate (PIP3).
source: PI3K phosphorylates phosphatidylinositol (4,5) bisphosphate at the PM to form phosphatidylinositol (3,4,5) trisphosphate (PIP3).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PI3K function.

claim: Phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN) catalyses the reverse reaction of PI3K, converting PIP3 back to PIP2.
source: Phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN) catalyses the reverse reaction (Kabuyama et al., 1996; Lee et al., 2018; Maehama and Dixon, 1998; Myers et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: PIP3 recruits effectors such as PDPK1 and Akt via their pleckstrin homology (PH) domains.
source: PIP3 is a bioactive lipid that recruits effectors such as phosphoinositide-dependent protein kinase 1 (PDPK1) and Akt via their pleckstrin homology (PH) domains, leading to their accumulation at the PM (Currie et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: PIP3 recruitment of PDPK1 and Akt leads to their accumulation at the plasma membrane.
source: PIP3 is a bioactive lipid that recruits effectors such as phosphoinositide-dependent protein kinase 1 (PDPK1) and Akt via their pleckstrin homology (PH) domains, leading to their accumulation at the PM (Currie et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Akt is phosphorylated at T309 (in Akt2; T308 in Akt1, T305 in Akt3) by PDPK1 at the plasma membrane.
source: Here, Akt is phosphorylated at T309 (in Akt2; T308 in Akt1, T305 in Akt3) by PDPK1 and S474 (in Akt2; S473 in Akt1, S472 in Akt3) by mammalian target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2) (Alessi et al., 1996a; Sarbassov et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Akt is phosphorylated at S474 (in Akt2; S473 in Akt1, S472 in Akt3) by mammalian target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2) at the plasma membrane.
source: Here, Akt is phosphorylated at T309 (in Akt2; T308 in Akt1, T305 in Akt3) by PDPK1 and S474 (in Akt2; S473 in Akt1, S472 in Akt3) by mammalian target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2) (Alessi et al., 1996a; Sarbassov et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Phosphorylation at T309 and S474 leads to full activation of Akt kinase activity.
source: This leads to full activation of Akt kinase activity (Kearney et al., 2019), and substrate phosphorylation ensues.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: More than 100 substrates of Akt have been reported.
source: More than 100 substrates of Akt have been reported, which regulate a myriad of biological pathways (Manning and Toker, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Dysregulated PI3K/Akt activity is linked to several diseases including cancer and type 2 diabetes.
source: Importantly, dysregulated PI3K/Akt activity is linked to several diseases including cancer and type 2 diabetes (Fruman et al., 2017), making tight regulation essential.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Insulin-stimulated recruitment of Akt to the plasma membrane displays overshoot behaviour.
source: Insulin-stimulated recruitment of Akt to the PM displays overshoot behaviour (a response where the initial maxima exceeds the final steady state) and oscillations (Ebner et al., 2017; Norris et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work and data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Insulin-stimulated recruitment of Akt to the plasma membrane displays oscillations.
source: Insulin-stimulated recruitment of Akt to the PM displays overshoot behaviour (a response where the initial maxima exceeds the final steady state) and oscillations (Ebner et al., 2017; Norris et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The overshoot and oscillatory dynamics of Akt recruitment are indicative of acute negative feedback signals that regulate Akt activation.
source: These dynamics are indicative of acute negative feedback signals that regulate Akt activation (Behar and Hoffmann, 2010; Cheong and Levchenko, 2010; Nyman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on established knowledge about feedback dynamics, supported by citations.

claim: mTORC1 and S6-kinase (S6K) are activated downstream of Akt.
source: mTORC1 and S6-kinase (S6K) are activated downstream of Akt (Manning and Toker, 2017), and have been reported to put the 'brakes' on PI3K/Akt signalling through a variety of mechanisms.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: mTORC1/S6K phosphorylates the mTORC2 component RICTOR to attenuate mTORC2 activity and hence Akt activity.
source: For example, mTORC1/S6K phosphorylates the mTORC2 component RICTOR to attenuate mTORC2 activity and hence Akt activity (Dibble et al., 2009; Julien et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: mTORC1/S6K-mediated phosphorylation of IRS1 limits PI3K/Akt activation.
source: Furthermore, mTORC1/S6K-mediated phosphorylation of IRS1 limits PI3K/Akt activation (Copps and White, 2012; Hançer et al., 2014; Harrington et al., 2004; Shah et al., 2004; Shah and Hunter, 2006; Tzatsos, 2009; Tzatsos and Kandror, 2006; Yoneyama et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: It remains unclear whether mTORC1/S6K feedbacks are responsible for the overshoot and oscillatory behaviour in Akt activation.
source: However, it remains unclear whether these feedbacks are responsible for the overshoot and oscillatory behaviour in Akt activation.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: In response to 1 nM insulin, plasma membrane levels of Akt reached a maximum at 75 s post-insulin stimulation.
source: Specifically, PM levels of Akt reached a maximum at 75 s post-insulin stimulation, followed by a rapid decline that reached a new steady state that was roughly half of its maximum by 10 min post-stimulation (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Following the maximum at 75 s, plasma membrane Akt levels rapidly declined to a new steady state that was roughly half of its maximum by 10 min post-stimulation with 1 nM insulin.
source: Specifically, PM levels of Akt reached a maximum at 75 s post-insulin stimulation, followed by a rapid decline that reached a new steady state that was roughly half of its maximum by 10 min post-stimulation (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In response to 100 nM insulin, the maximum recruitment of Akt was fourfold higher than 1 nM insulin.
source: In response to 100 nM insulin, the maximum recruitment of Akt was fourfold higher than 1 nM insulin, with an initial overshoot followed by a secondary increase (Figure 1B), which may reflect the engagement of a positive feedback signal at this dose.
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The secondary increase in Akt recruitment at 100 nM insulin may reflect the engagement of a positive feedback signal at this dose.
source: In response to 100 nM insulin, the maximum recruitment of Akt was fourfold higher than 1 nM insulin, with an initial overshoot followed by a secondary increase (Figure 1B), which may reflect the engagement of a positive feedback signal at this dose.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed data.

claim: The overshoot in Akt recruitment is reflected in its activation as measured by phosphorylation at T309 and S474.
source: A similar overshoot was observed for insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of Akt at its activating sites T309 and S474 (Figure 1C,D), indicating that the overshoot in Akt recruitment is reflected in its activation.
evidence: This is supported by the western blot data in Figure 1C,D.

claim: The kinetics of T309 phosphorylation were much faster than S474 phosphorylation.
source: The kinetics of T309 phosphorylation were much faster than S474 phosphorylation.
evidence: This is observed in the data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: The phosphorylation of Akt substrates (AS160, FOXO1, GSK3, and PRAS40) did not exhibit an overshoot.
source: Interestingly the phosphorylation of Akt substrates (AS160, FOXO1, GSK3, and PRAS40) did not exhibit an overshoot (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is observed in the western blot data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: Akt singly phosphorylated at T309 is active.
source: Although Akt singly phosphorylated at T309 is active, the delayed onset of S474 phosphorylation doubles Akt activity (Kearney et al., 2019) and likely extends the peak phosphorylation observed for these substrates.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The delayed onset of S474 phosphorylation doubles Akt activity.
source: Although Akt singly phosphorylated at T309 is active, the delayed onset of S474 phosphorylation doubles Akt activity (Kearney et al., 2019) and likely extends the peak phosphorylation observed for these substrates.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The delayed onset of S474 phosphorylation likely extends the peak phosphorylation observed for Akt substrates.
source: Although Akt singly phosphorylated at T309 is active, the delayed onset of S474 phosphorylation doubles Akt activity (Kearney et al., 2019) and likely extends the peak phosphorylation observed for these substrates.
evidence: This is an inference based on the kinetics of S474 phosphorylation and substrate phosphorylation.

claim: The computational model predicted a loss of the overshoot and a 25% increase in the recruitment of Akt to the plasma membrane in the presence of rapamycin with 1 nM insulin.
source: The model predicted a loss of the overshoot and a 25% increase in the recruitment of Akt to the PM (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a prediction from the computational model shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Despite complete inhibition of mTORC1 activity by rapamycin, no change was observed in Akt recruitment.
source: Despite complete inhibition of mTORC1 activity by rapamycin, no change was observed in either Akt recruitment (Figure 1G) or phosphorylation (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 1G,H.

claim: Despite complete inhibition of mTORC1 activity by rapamycin, no change was observed in Akt phosphorylation.
source: Despite complete inhibition of mTORC1 activity by rapamycin, no change was observed in either Akt recruitment (Figure 1G) or phosphorylation (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The data point to a feedback mechanism during the early insulin response that drives the overshoot in Akt recruitment that is independent of mTORC1.
source: Together, these data point to a feedback mechanism during the early insulin response that drives the overshoot in Akt recruitment that is independent of mTORC1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the rapamycin experiments and modeling results.

claim: Model 9 (Akt to IRS/PI3K) best matched the experimental data among the tested models.
source: Quantitative assessment of model fitting based on the objective function revealed that Akt to IRS/PI3K (model 9) best matched the experimental data, followed by mTORC2 to PTEN (model 7), and then Akt to PTEN (model 8) (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on quantitative model fitting shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In the presence of GDC0068, a threefold increase in Akt recruitment to the plasma membrane was observed upon insulin stimulation and loss of overshoot.
source: Strikingly, in the presence of GDC0068, we observed a threefold increase in Akt recruitment to the PM upon insulin stimulation and loss of overshoot (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Subcellular fractionation showed a marked potentiation of insulin-stimulated Akt2 recruitment to the plasma membrane in the presence of GDC0068.
source: These data were corroborated by assessment of endogenous Akt localisation in adipocytes using subcellular fractionation, which showed a marked potentiation of insulin-stimulated Akt2 recruitment to the PM in the presence of GDC0068 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The phenomenon of increased Akt recruitment with Akt inhibition was not specific to adipocytes, but rather a common feature of multiple cell types – HEK293E, HeLa, 3T3-L1 fibroblasts, and MCF7 cells.
source: This phenomenon was not specific to adipocytes, but rather a common feature of multiple cell types – HEK293E, HeLa, 3T3-L1 fibroblasts, and MCF7 cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B–E).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B–E.

claim: Both W80A-T309A-S474A and W80A-K181A kinase-dead Akt mutants exhibited 3.5-fold augmented recruitment and loss of overshoot behaviour compared to W80A Akt.
source: Both mutants exhibited 3.5-fold augmented recruitment and loss of overshoot behaviour compared to W80A Akt (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The data indicate the presence of an Akt-dependent feedback signal which limits its activation at the plasma membrane, likely through the IRS/PI3K node.
source: Taken together, these data indicate the presence of an Akt-dependent feedback signal which limits its activation at the PM, likely through the IRS/PI3K node.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling and experimental data.

claim: Loss of S474 phosphorylation resulted in an attenuated overshoot in response to 1 nM insulin but no difference in response magnitude compared to control.
source: Loss of S474 phosphorylation resulted in an attenuated overshoot in response to 1 nM insulin but no difference in response magnitude compared to control.
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: W80A-T309A Akt displayed a loss of overshoot and a threefold increase in plasma membrane association in comparison to control in response to 1 nM insulin.
source: In response to 1 nM insulin, W80A-T309A Akt displayed a loss of overshoot and a threefold increase in PM association in comparison to control (Figure 2I).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: The phosphorylation of Akt at S474 is largely redundant in activating the negative feedback.
source: These combined modelling and experimental analyses support that the phosphorylation of Akt at S474 is largely redundant in activating the negative feedback.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling predictions and experimental data with S474A mutant.

claim: Each Akt inhibitor (GDC0068, MK2206, GSK2334470) augmented insulin-stimulated PIP3 abundance approximately fivefold relative to insulin alone.
source: Strikingly, each inhibitor further augmented insulin-stimulated PIP3 abundance approximately fivefold relative to insulin alone (Figure 3A), suggesting that Akt regulates PIP3 abundance.
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Akt regulates PIP3 abundance.
source: Strikingly, each inhibitor further augmented insulin-stimulated PIP3 abundance approximately fivefold relative to insulin alone (Figure 3A), suggesting that Akt regulates PIP3 abundance.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Akt inhibition increases PIP3 levels.

claim: The degree of PDPK1 recruitment to the plasma membrane was markedly enhanced with GDC0068 and MK2206.
source: Furthermore, their degree of recruitment was markedly enhanced with GDC0068 and MK2206 (Figure 3B–D), consistent with increased PIP3 in the absence of Akt activity.
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The degree of Gab2PH recruitment to the plasma membrane was markedly enhanced with GDC0068 and MK2206.
source: Furthermore, their degree of recruitment was markedly enhanced with GDC0068 and MK2206 (Figure 3B–D), consistent with increased PIP3 in the absence of Akt activity.
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 3C,D.

claim: MK2206-dependent hyper-recruitment of Gab2PH-eGFP was rescued by co-expression of W80A Akt, but not WT or W80A-T309A Akt.
source: In the presence of MK2206, the Akt constructs behaved as expected (Figure 3E), while MK2206-dependent hyper-recruitment of Gab2PH-eGFP was rescued by co-expression of W80A Akt, but not WT or W80A-T309A Akt (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Akt regulates PIP3 abundance and this alters the localisation of PIP3-binding proteins.
source: These data suggest that Akt regulates PIP3 abundance and this alters the localisation of PIP3-binding proteins.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments showing altered recruitment of PDPK1 and Gab2PH with Akt inhibition.

claim: There was no difference in the rate of plasma membrane dissociation between W80A (active) and W80A-T309A (kinase-dead) Akt following PI3K inhibition.
source: There was no difference in their rate of PM dissociation, consistent with the Akt to IRS/PI3K negative feedback model (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Regardless of whether Akt was inhibited, there was no difference in the rate of PDPK1 plasma membrane dissociation following PI3K inhibition.
source: Regardless of whether Akt was inhibited, there was no difference in the rate of PDPK1 PM dissociation (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: In cells expressing constitutively active PI3K (p110*), there was no increase in W80A-T309A Akt recruitment when stimulated with MK2206, indicating no loss of feedback.
source: When stimulated with MK2206, there was no increase in W80A-T309A Akt recruitment, indicating no loss of feedback (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: In HCC1937 PTEN-null cells, Akt recruitment increased in response to IGF1 and increased further with GDC0068.
source: Akt recruitment increased in response to IGF1 and increased further with GDC0068 (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Akt-mediated feedback is engaged in the absence of PTEN.
source: This was consistent with the engagement of Akt-mediated feedback in the absence of PTEN.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Akt inhibition increases recruitment even in PTEN-null cells.

claim: Subcellular fractionation revealed an increase in the abundance of PI3K p85 and p110 at the plasma membrane upon insulin stimulation, which was potentiated in the presence of Akt inhibitors GDC0068 and MK2206.
source: Subcellular fractionation revealed an increase in the abundance of PI3K p85 and p110 at the PM upon insulin stimulation, which was potentiated in the presence of Akt inhibitors GDC0068 and MK2206 (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Immunofluorescence/TIRFM showed an increase in plasma membrane localised PI3K p85 in the presence of the Akt inhibitors GDC0068 and MK2206.
source: These data were corroborated by assessment of PI3K p85 localisation using immunofluorescence/TIRFM. This technique was less sensitive than subcellular fractionation, as it did not reveal a change in PM localised PI3K with 1 nM insulin; however, an increase was detectable in the presence of the Akt inhibitors GDC0068 and MK2206 (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Upon acute growth factor stimulation, Akt translocates to the plasma membrane where it is phosphorylated and activated, then engages a negative feedback mechanism that limits plasma membrane-associated PI3K and consequently lowers PIP3 abundance.
source: Together, these data are consistent with the Akt to IRS/PI3K negative feedback model. Specifically, upon acute growth factor stimulation, Akt translocates to the PM where it is phosphorylated and activated. Akt then engages a negative feedback mechanism that limits PM-associated PI3K and consequently lowers PIP3 abundance.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claim: Following insulin stimulation, the amount of IRS1 at the plasma membrane decreased.
source: Following insulin stimulation, the amount of IRS1/2 at the PM decreased (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Following insulin stimulation, the amount of IRS2 at the plasma membrane decreased.
source: Following insulin stimulation, the amount of IRS1/2 at the PM decreased (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In the presence of Akt inhibitors (GDC0068 and MK2206), IRS1 was retained at the plasma membrane following insulin stimulation.
source: However, in the presence of Akt inhibitors (GDC0068 and MK2206), IRS1/2 were retained at the PM (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: In the presence of Akt inhibitors (GDC0068 and MK2206), IRS2 was retained at the plasma membrane following insulin stimulation.
source: However, in the presence of Akt inhibitors (GDC0068 and MK2206), IRS1/2 were retained at the PM (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Rapamycin was unable to inhibit the insulin-stimulated decrease in plasma membrane-associated IRS1.
source: Importantly, rapamycin was unable to inhibit the insulin-stimulated decrease in PM-associated IRS1/2 (Figure 5C,D), demonstrating that this process is mTORC1/S6K-independent.
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Rapamycin was unable to inhibit the insulin-stimulated decrease in plasma membrane-associated IRS2.
source: Importantly, rapamycin was unable to inhibit the insulin-stimulated decrease in PM-associated IRS1/2 (Figure 5C,D), demonstrating that this process is mTORC1/S6K-independent.
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The insulin-stimulated decrease in plasma membrane-associated IRS1/2 is mTORC1/S6K-independent.
source: Importantly, rapamycin was unable to inhibit the insulin-stimulated decrease in PM-associated IRS1/2 (Figure 5C,D), demonstrating that this process is mTORC1/S6K-independent.
evidence: This is concluded from the rapamycin experiments.

claim: Subcellular fractionation demonstrated an Akt-dependent decrease in the abundance of endogenous IRS1 at the plasma membrane upon insulin stimulation.
source: Consistent with these observations, subcellular fractionation also demonstrated an Akt-dependent decrease in the abundance of endogenous IRS1 at the PM and extended these findings to reveal that IRS1 moves from the PM to the cytosol upon insulin stimulation, rather than to internal membranes (high density microsome [HDM]/low density microsome [LDM] fractions) (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: IRS1 moves from the plasma membrane to the cytosol upon insulin stimulation, rather than to internal membranes.
source: Consistent with these observations, subcellular fractionation also demonstrated an Akt-dependent decrease in the abundance of endogenous IRS1 at the PM and extended these findings to reveal that IRS1 moves from the PM to the cytosol upon insulin stimulation, rather than to internal membranes (high density microsome [HDM]/low density microsome [LDM] fractions) (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Deletion of the IRS1 PH domain decreased its abundance at the plasma membrane in unstimulated cells.
source: We attribute the PM localisation of IRS1/2 prior to insulin stimulation to its PH domain, as deletion of the IRS1 PH domain (DelPH IRS1-eGFP) decreased its abundance at the PM in unstimulated cells (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The plasma membrane localisation of IRS1/2 prior to insulin stimulation is due to its PH domain.
source: We attribute the PM localisation of IRS1/2 prior to insulin stimulation to its PH domain, as deletion of the IRS1 PH domain (DelPH IRS1-eGFP) decreased its abundance at the PM in unstimulated cells (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that deletion of the PH domain reduces PM localization.

claim: IRS1/2 is plasma membrane-localised in unstimulated cells via a PH domain-dependent interaction.
source: Together, these data indicate that IRS1/2 is PM-localised in unstimulated cells via a PH domain-dependent interaction, and upon insulin stimulation Akt induces the translocation of IRS1/2 from the PM to the cytosol.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments with DelPH IRS1.

claim: Upon insulin stimulation Akt induces the translocation of IRS1/2 from the plasma membrane to the cytosol.
source: Together, these data indicate that IRS1/2 is PM-localised in unstimulated cells via a PH domain-dependent interaction, and upon insulin stimulation Akt induces the translocation of IRS1/2 from the PM to the cytosol.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments showing Akt-dependent IRS translocation.

claim: Treatment with Akt inhibitors did not alter insulin receptor localisation.
source: Consistent with direct regulation of IRS by Akt, treatment with Akt inhibitors did not alter IR localisation (Figure 5G) or activation as measured by tyrosine phosphorylation (Figure 5H).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Treatment with Akt inhibitors did not alter insulin receptor activation as measured by tyrosine phosphorylation.
source: Consistent with direct regulation of IRS by Akt, treatment with Akt inhibitors did not alter IR localisation (Figure 5G) or activation as measured by tyrosine phosphorylation (Figure 5H).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Deletion of the PTB domain of IRS1 did not impact IRS1 removal from the plasma membrane upon insulin stimulation.
source: Furthermore, deletion of the PTB domain of IRS1 (DelPTB IRS1-eGFP), which is responsible for its interaction with the IR (Eck et al., 1996), did not impact IRS1 removal from the PM upon insulin stimulation (Figure 5I).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Akt removes IRS from the plasma membrane via disruption of insulin receptor-independent interactions.
source: These data suggest that Akt removes IRS from the PM via disruption of IR-independent interactions.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that DelPTB IRS1 still translocates from the PM.

claim: The insulin receptor was only detected in IRS1 immunoprecipitates in the presence of insulin.
source: Following immunoprecipitation of endogenous IRS1 or IRS2 followed by mass spectrometry, the IR was only detected in the presence of insulin, consistent with a strong insulin-dependent interaction (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 5J.

claim: The insulin receptor was only detected in IRS2 immunoprecipitates in the presence of insulin.
source: Following immunoprecipitation of endogenous IRS1 or IRS2 followed by mass spectrometry, the IR was only detected in the presence of insulin, consistent with a strong insulin-dependent interaction (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 5J.

claim: The amount of insulin receptor detected in IRS1 immunoprecipitates was augmented in the presence of Akt inhibitors GDC0068 and MK2206 (approximately 17- and 7-fold, respectively).
source: However, the amount of IR detected was augmented in the presence of Akt inhibitors GDC0068 and MK2206 (approximately 17- and 7-fold for IRS1; 19- and 12-fold for IRS2, respectively; Figure 5J), suggesting that Akt controls the level of interaction between the IR and IRS.
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 5J.

claim: The amount of insulin receptor detected in IRS2 immunoprecipitates was augmented in the presence of Akt inhibitors GDC0068 and MK2206 (approximately 19- and 12-fold, respectively).
source: However, the amount of IR detected was augmented in the presence of Akt inhibitors GDC0068 and MK2206 (approximately 17- and 7-fold for IRS1; 19- and 12-fold for IRS2, respectively; Figure 5J), suggesting that Akt controls the level of interaction between the IR and IRS.
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 5J.

claim: Akt controls the level of interaction between the insulin receptor and IRS.
source: However, the amount of IR detected was augmented in the presence of Akt inhibitors GDC0068 and MK2206 (approximately 17- and 7-fold for IRS1; 19- and 12-fold for IRS2, respectively; Figure 5J), suggesting that Akt controls the level of interaction between the IR and IRS.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Akt inhibition increases IR-IRS interaction.

claim: Akt limits PI3K-mediated PIP3 production by depleting plasma membrane-associated IRS, to reduce the pool of IRS available to interact with activated insulin receptor.
source: These data suggest that Akt limits PI3K-mediated PIP3 production by depleting PM-associated IRS, to reduce the pool of IRS available to interact with activated IR.
evidence: This is the main conclusion about the mechanism, supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claim: Collectively, IRS1 and IRS2 contained 11 phosphorylation sites within an Akt substrate motif (R-X-R-X-X-S/T).
source: Collectively, IRS1 and IRS2 contained 11 phosphorylation sites within an Akt substrate motif (R-X-R-X-X-S/T) (Alessi et al., 1996b).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and established knowledge of the Akt substrate motif.

claim: Following insulin stimulation, wild-type IRS1 dissociated from the plasma membrane.
source: Following insulin stimulation, WT IRS1/2 dissociated from the PM; however, increased PM abundance was observed for both 6P IRS1 and 5P IRS2 (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Following insulin stimulation, wild-type IRS2 dissociated from the plasma membrane.
source: Following insulin stimulation, WT IRS1/2 dissociated from the PM; however, increased PM abundance was observed for both 6P IRS1 and 5P IRS2 (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Following insulin stimulation, increased plasma membrane abundance was observed for 6P IRS1 (with six Akt motif sites mutated to alanine).
source: Following insulin stimulation, WT IRS1/2 dissociated from the PM; however, increased PM abundance was observed for both 6P IRS1 and 5P IRS2 (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Following insulin stimulation, increased plasma membrane abundance was observed for 5P IRS2 (with five Akt motif sites mutated to alanine).
source: Following insulin stimulation, WT IRS1/2 dissociated from the PM; however, increased PM abundance was observed for both 6P IRS1 and 5P IRS2 (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Expression of 6P IRS1 in adipocytes resulted in hyper-recruitment of Akt to the plasma membrane compared to cells expressing wild-type IRS1.
source: Furthermore, expression of 6P IRS1 or 5P IRS2 in adipocytes resulted in hyper-recruitment of Akt to the PM compared to cells expressing WT IRS (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Expression of 5P IRS2 in adipocytes resulted in hyper-recruitment of Akt to the plasma membrane compared to cells expressing wild-type IRS2.
source: Furthermore, expression of 6P IRS1 or 5P IRS2 in adipocytes resulted in hyper-recruitment of Akt to the PM compared to cells expressing WT IRS (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Phosphorylation of IRS1/2 facilitates its removal from the plasma membrane and drives negative feedback.
source: These data suggest that phosphorylation of IRS1/2 facilitates its removal from the PM and drives negative feedback.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments with 6P IRS1 and 5P IRS2 mutants.

claim: IRS2 S306 (S303 in mouse) can be phosphorylated by Akt in vitro.
source: However, IRS2 S306 (S303 in mouse) and S577 (S573 in mouse) were phosphorylated by Akt in vitro, and in cells were sensitive to GDC0068/MK2206, but not rapamycin/rapalink (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: This is directly observed in the mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: IRS2 S577 (S573 in mouse) can be phosphorylated by Akt in vitro.
source: However, IRS2 S306 (S303 in mouse) and S577 (S573 in mouse) were phosphorylated by Akt in vitro, and in cells were sensitive to GDC0068/MK2206, but not rapamycin/rapalink (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: This is directly observed in the mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: In cells, IRS2 S306 phosphorylation was sensitive to GDC0068/MK2206, but not rapamycin/rapalink.
source: However, IRS2 S306 (S303 in mouse) and S577 (S573 in mouse) were phosphorylated by Akt in vitro, and in cells were sensitive to GDC0068/MK2206, but not rapamycin/rapalink (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: This is directly observed in the mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: In cells, IRS2 S577 phosphorylation was sensitive to GDC0068/MK2206, but not rapamycin/rapalink.
source: However, IRS2 S306 (S303 in mouse) and S577 (S573 in mouse) were phosphorylated by Akt in vitro, and in cells were sensitive to GDC0068/MK2206, but not rapamycin/rapalink (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: This is directly observed in the mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: IRS2 S306 and S577 are novel Akt substrates.
source: These data were sufficient to classify IRS2 S306 and S577 as novel Akt substrates.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in vitro kinase assays and cellular experiments with Akt and mTORC1 inhibitors.

claim: Concurrent mutation of IRS2 S306 and S577 to alanine (S306/577A IRS2) prevented plasma membrane dissociation of IRS2 following insulin stimulation.
source: However, concurrent mutation of both phosphorylation sites (S306/577A IRS2) prevented PM dissociation of IRS2 (Figure 6G), mimicking Akt inhibition with GDC0068 and MK2206 (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Expression of S306/577A IRS2 resulted in hyper-recruitment of Akt to the plasma membrane compared to cells expressing wild-type IRS2.
source: Furthermore, expression of S306/577A IRS2 resulted in hyper-recruitment of Akt and PDPK1 to the PM compared to cells expressing WT IRS2 (Figure 6G,H), consistent with increased PIP3 levels.
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Expression of S306/577A IRS2 resulted in hyper-recruitment of PDPK1 to the plasma membrane compared to cells expressing wild-type IRS2.
source: Furthermore, expression of S306/577A IRS2 resulted in hyper-recruitment of Akt and PDPK1 to the PM compared to cells expressing WT IRS2 (Figure 6G,H), consistent with increased PIP3 levels.
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Akt-mediated phosphorylation of IRS2 S306 and S577 synergistically dissociates plasma membrane-associated IRS2 to limit PIP3 production and Akt activation.
source: These data suggest that Akt-mediated phosphorylation of IRS2 S306 and S577 synergistically dissociates PM-associated IRS2 to limit PIP3 production and Akt activation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments with S306/577A IRS2 mutant.

claim: Mutation of the corresponding phosphorylation sites in IRS1 (S270/527A) did not prevent its dissociation from the plasma membrane upon insulin stimulation.
source: Intriguingly, mutation of the corresponding phosphorylation sites in IRS1 (S270/527A) did not prevent its dissociation from the PM upon insulin stimulation and only had a subtle effect on Akt recruitment (Figure 6—figure supplement 4), demonstrating alternate regulation between the IRS isoforms.
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4.

claim: There is alternate regulation between the IRS1 and IRS2 isoforms.
source: Intriguingly, mutation of the corresponding phosphorylation sites in IRS1 (S270/527A) did not prevent its dissociation from the PM upon insulin stimulation and only had a subtle effect on Akt recruitment (Figure 6—figure supplement 4), demonstrating alternate regulation between the IRS isoforms.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of mutations in IRS1 vs IRS2.

claim: In unstimulated cells, a pool of IRS is localised to the plasma membrane via a PH domain-dependent interaction.
source: We propose a model where in unstimulated cells, a pool of IRS is localised to the PM via a PH domain-dependent interaction.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claim: Upon insulin binding its receptor, Akt is rapidly activated by the canonical IRS/PI3K pathway and directly phosphorylates IRS proteins at key regulatory residues such as IRS2 S306 and S577.
source: Upon insulin binding its receptor, Akt is rapidly activated (by the canonical IRS/PI3K pathway) and directly phosphorylates IRS proteins at key regulatory residues such as IRS2 S306 and S577.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claim: Akt phosphorylation of IRS results in the translocation of IRS from the plasma membrane to the cytosol and depletes the pool available to interact with the insulin receptor.
source: This results in the translocation of IRS from the PM to the cytosol and depletes the pool available to interact with the IR.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claim: Akt phosphorylation of IRS ultimately limits plasma membrane-associated PI3K and PIP3 synthesis.
source: Ultimately, these events limit PM-associated PI3K and PIP3 synthesis (Figure 7).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings, illustrated in Figure 7.

claim: The described feedback mechanism may have co-evolved with IRS proteins as an obligate intermediate between the insulin receptor and PI3K to enhance the signalling capacity of the insulin receptor.
source: We envisage that the described feedback mechanism may have co-evolved with IRS proteins as an obligate intermediate between the IR and PI3K to enhance the signalling capacity of the IR in several ways.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation about the evolutionary significance of the mechanism.

claim: The feedback mechanism may provide the basis for more precise temporal control of insulin signalling.
source: First, it may provide the basis for more precise temporal control of insulin signalling.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation about the functional significance of the mechanism.

claim: The feedback mechanism provides means to specifically regulate insulin signalling whilst keeping PI3K activation by other signalling pathways intact.
source: Second, it provides means to specifically regulate insulin signalling whilst keeping PI3K activation by other signalling pathways intact.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation about the functional significance of the mechanism.

claim: The described mechanism may enable crosstalk between different growth factor pathways through IRS phosphorylation by a range of other kinases.
source: Finally, as IRS1/2 can be phosphorylated by a range of other kinases (Copps and White, 2012), it is possible that the described mechanism transcends to other kinases and enables crosstalk between different growth factor pathways.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation about the broader significance of the mechanism.

claim: The feedback signal reported in this study does not need mTORC1 activation.
source: However, the feedback signal reported here does not need mTORC1 activation; rapamycin had no effect on acute Akt recruitment, phosphorylation (Figure 1G,H), or IRS1/2 localisation (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the rapamycin experiments.

claim: The Akt-derived feedback signal is activated acutely (~1 min) following growth factor exposure.
source: Rather, our data suggest an Akt-derived feedback signal that is activated acutely (~1 min) following growth factor exposure.
evidence: This is based on the kinetics observed in the experimental data.

claim: Negative feedbacks emanating from mTORC1/S6K are much slower than the negative feedback described in this study.
source: We suspect that described negative feedbacks emanating from mTORC1/S6K are much slower than the negative feedback described in this study, particularly those that rely on the degradation of IRS.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the kinetics of the observed feedback and known mechanisms of mTORC1/S6K feedback.

claim: In the absence of S474 phosphorylation, Akt is active and sustains T309 phosphorylation.
source: Recent findings by our lab and others have shown that in the absence of S474 phosphorylation, Akt is active and sustains T309 phosphorylation (Beg et al., 2017; Jacinto et al., 2006; Kearney et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Negative feedback is engaged in the absence of S474 phosphorylation.
source: Indeed, here we show that negative feedback is engaged in the absence of S474 phosphorylation (Figure 2I).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Akt phosphorylated at T309 alone is capable of substrate phosphorylation and sufficient for eliciting feedback mechanisms.
source: Collectively these findings demonstrate that Akt phosphorylated at T309, but not S474 is capable of substrate phosphorylation and sufficient for eliciting feedback mechanisms.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments with S474A mutant and previous work.

claim: Losing negative feedback from Akt to IRS resulted in a profound increase in PIP3 levels.
source: Losing negative feedback from Akt to IRS resulted in a profound increase in PIP3 levels (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Hyperactivation of Akt due to upstream genetic lesions (e.g., PI3K, PTEN) or mutation in Akt itself (e.g., E17K) can result in uncontrolled regulation of processes such as cell proliferation and survival.
source: Hyperactivation of Akt due to upstream genetic lesions (e.g., PI3K, PTEN) or mutation in Akt itself (e.g., E17K) can result in uncontrolled regulation of processes such as cell proliferation and survival (Altomare and Testa, 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Akt is frequently hyperactivated in human cancers.
source: As Akt is frequently hyperactivated in human cancers, it has been the target of numerous cancer therapeutics.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: No Akt inhibitors have been approved for use despite the perceived potential.
source: However, despite the perceived potential, no Akt inhibitors have been approved for use (Nitulescu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Akt inhibitors such as MK2206 and GDC0068 have been tested in clinical trials but severe side effects were experienced and substantial tumour shrinkage was generally not observed.
source: Akt inhibitors such as MK2206 and GDC0068 have been tested in clinical trials; however, severe side effects were experienced and substantial tumour shrinkage was generally not observed (Saura et al., 2017; Xing et al., 2019; Yap et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Therapeutic targeting of kinases such as Akt can have unexpected effects on other signalling networks, resulting from loss of feedback and crosstalk.
source: The data presented herein demonstrate that the therapeutic targeting of kinases such as Akt can have unexpected effects on other signalling networks, resulting from loss of feedback and crosstalk.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings showing increased PIP3 and altered signaling with Akt inhibition.

claim: Inhibition of Akt increased insulin-stimulated PIP3 levels by more than fivefold.
source: For example, inhibition of Akt increased insulin-stimulated PIP3 levels by more than fivefold (Figure 3A) and enhanced PM recruitment of PH domain containing proteins PDPK1 and GAB2 (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Inhibition of Akt enhanced plasma membrane recruitment of PH domain containing proteins PDPK1 and GAB2.
source: For example, inhibition of Akt increased insulin-stimulated PIP3 levels by more than fivefold (Figure 3A) and enhanced PM recruitment of PH domain containing proteins PDPK1 and GAB2 (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This is directly observed in the experimental data shown in Figure 3B-D.

claim: PDPK1 is the master regulator of other kinases such as PKC, S6K, and SGK.
source: PDPK1 is the master regulator of other kinases such as PKC, S6K, and SGK, and so PDPK1 mislocalisation at the PM would likely influence these networks.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: PDPK1 mislocalisation at the plasma membrane would likely influence PKC, S6K, and SGK networks.
source: PDPK1 is the master regulator of other kinases such as PKC, S6K, and SGK, and so PDPK1 mislocalisation at the PM would likely influence these networks.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known role of PDPK1.

claim: The central importance of PIP3 beyond Akt signalling may have contributed to the lack of efficacy Akt inhibitors have had in the clinic.
source: Thus, the central importance of PIP3 beyond Akt signalling (Czech, 2000) may have contributed to the lack of efficacy Akt inhibitors have had in the clinic.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the experimental findings and clinical observations.

claim: A more detailed understanding of feedback and crosstalk across signalling networks is needed in order to generate effective therapeutics.
source: These data highlight the need for a more detailed understanding of feedback and crosstalk across signalling networks in order to generate effective therapeutics.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the implications of the study for drug development.
